recommendations.headline: Customer satisfaction, not price, is the real conversion lever: satisfied calls close at 72% versus 16% for neutral and just 6% for dissatisfied calls, yet 52% of all 2,213 calls end merely 'neutral' and reps leave basic closing steps undone (208 calls didn't even ask for the order).
behaviour: Price enquiry dominates intent (755/2,213 = 34%) but price is rarely resolved on the call: 1,550 of 2,213 calls (70%) never reach a price_reaction stage, only 245 (11%) end in accepted price.
Callback is the most common outcome by far (1,006/2,213 = 45%), nearly 2.5x actual orders (429 = 19%), showing heavy reliance on follow-up rather than same-call closing.

Comparison shopping is widespread: price_shopper (381), comparing_quotes (232) and indecisive (142) behaviours together touch roughly a third of tracked behaviours, and competitor_cheaper is cited in 80 calls with only 24% win rate.
Stock and speed matter as much as price: fast_delivery (411) and stock_availability (402) are the top two stated needs, and stock_availability is the #2 objection (301 calls, 25% win rate).

Dealers are the core customer base (1,071/2,213 = 48% of calls) and convert best among big segments (40% win), while the 795 'unknown' segment calls (36%) convert worst (25%), pointing to a segment-capture gap.
satisfaction: Win rate tracks satisfaction almost perfectly: satisfied 72%, neutral 16%, dissatisfied 6%, unknown 11% — satisfaction is the single strongest predictor of an order in this data.
Only 772 of 2,213 calls (35%) are rated satisfied; the majority, 1,159 (52%), are neutral — a large pool that could be shifted to 'satisfied' with better call handling.

Price is rarely the deal-breaker in raw numbers: only 71 calls (3%) end 'too_high' and price_high objection still wins 28% of the time, while stock_availability (25%) and competitor_cheaper (24%) win rates are just as weak or weaker.

Rep execution gaps directly depress satisfaction: slow_or_unclear_answer (370 calls, 17%) and no_follow_up_fixed (344, 16%) are the top two missed actions, both of which are controllable without touching price.

conversion.title: Close the satisfaction gap on neutral calls
conversion.evidence: Neutral calls (1,159, 52% of total) convert at only 16% vs 72% for satisfied calls.
conversion.action: Train reps to actively confirm customer satisfaction before ending the call (summarise next steps, ask 'does this work for you?') rather than letting calls end flat.

conversion.title: Always ask for the order
conversion.evidence: 208 calls had no closing ask despite order intent appearing in 483 calls and interested outcome in 330 calls.
conversion.action: Mandate a direct close line ('Shall I book this for you?') on every price/product enquiry call; add it to call-quality checklist.

conversion.title: Send the quote during the call, not later
conversion.evidence: 207 calls had no quote sent, and many 'did not convert' summaries end in 'will send price list/photo later'.
conversion.action: Equip reps with ready rate cards/templates so a written quote or screenshot is shared before the call ends.

conversion.title: Fix stock-availability objection handling
conversion.evidence: Stock_availability is the 2nd-biggest objection (301 calls) with only 25% win rate; didnt_offer_alternative occurred 121 times.
conversion.action: Give reps a live/frequently-updated stock sheet and a pre-approved substitute list so an alternative is offered on the spot instead of 'will check and call back'.

conversion.title: Convert 'callback' into fixed commitments
conversion.evidence: Callback is the outcome in 1,006 of 2,213 calls (45%), and no_follow_up_fixed was flagged 344 times.
conversion.action: Require reps to set and log a specific date/time for follow-up before ending any callback-outcome call; manager to audit adherence weekly.

conversion.title: Capture segment on 'unknown' calls
conversion.evidence: Unknown segment is 795 calls (36%) with the lowest win rate (25%) versus dealer's 40%.
conversion.action: Add a mandatory segment-tagging question (dealer/fabricator/contractor/end-user) early in the call script.

conversion.title: Reframe price objections around value, not discount
conversion.evidence: Price_high is the top objection (309 calls, 14%) but still wins only 28%; didnt_highlight_value missed 76 times.
conversion.action: Coach reps to lead with quality/brand/delivery value points before any price discussion, per the non_price_benefits list.

offers.title: Pre-price-increase booking window
offers.why: Multiple 'went well' summaries show customers rushing to order ahead of announced 10% price increases (rods, screws, sheets).

offers.title: On-site cutting/processing service
offers.for_whom: Fabricators and contractors needing exact sizes
offers.why: Cutting_processing is a stated need in 93 calls, and several summaries involve bend/trim length clarifications.

offers.title: Committed delivery time-slot program
offers.why: Fast_delivery is the #1 need (411 calls) and delivery_time is the 3rd-highest objection (180 calls).

offers.title: Structured short-term credit for established dealers
offers.why: Needs_credit appears in 85 calls, credit_period need in 72, and credit_terms objection has the best win rate of all objections (30%), suggesting resolving it converts well.

offers.title: Standard sample/colour-card kit
offers.for_whom: First-time buyers and architects/builders choosing shades
offers.why: Samples need (58) and repeated requests for colour cards/shade photos across both converted and unconverted calls.

offers.title: Pre-approved alternate SKU list for stock-outs
offers.for_whom: Any customer facing an out-of-stock item
offers.why: Didnt_offer_alternative missed in 121 calls while stock_availability objection appears in 301 calls.

loyalty.title: Repeat-buyer recognition tier
loyalty.how: Flag repeat_buyer accounts in the system and give them a named contact/priority queue for calls and dispatch.
loyalty.why: Repeat_buyer behaviour logged 198 times but only 17 calls show loyal_to_us sentiment — conversion gap to close via recognition, not price.

loyalty.title: Formal referral tracking
loyalty.how: Log referral source on every call and acknowledge/thank referring customers with priority service.
loyalty.why: Referral behaviour noted in 26 calls; currently informal and untracked.

loyalty.title: Dedicated account contact for dealers
loyalty.how: Assign a single rep/manager per key dealer account for continuity across calls.
loyalty.why: Dealers are 1,071 of 2,213 calls (48%) and already the best-converting large segment (40% win) — consistency can push this higher.

loyalty.title: Proactive status-update messages
loyalty.how: Send automatic WhatsApp/SMS updates on order, dispatch and payment status without customer having to call in.
loyalty.why: Regular_updates need appears in 181 calls, and many 'did not convert' summaries are customers chasing dispatch/payment status themselves.

loyalty.title: Post-delivery check-in calls
loyalty.how: Schedule a short follow-up call after delivery to confirm quality and resolve issues early.
loyalty.why: Quality_doubt objection (90 calls) and after_sales_support need (40 calls) indicate a gap after the sale is made.

non_price_benefits.title: Authorised JSW distributor credibility
non_price_benefits.why: JSW is the most-mentioned competitor/brand reference (55 calls) and quality_doubt is an objection in 90 calls — lead with authorised-distributor status and test certificates (16 requests) to build trust.

non_price_benefits.title: Fast and reliable delivery track record
non_price_benefits.why: Fast_delivery is the top customer need (411 calls, 19%) — a concrete differentiator to state upfront on every call.

non_price_benefits.title: In-house technical advice
non_price_benefits.why: Needs_technical_help (328) and technical_advice (365, 16%) are among the top behaviours/needs — position reps as advisors on gauge, thickness and sizing, not just order-takers.

non_price_benefits.title: Consistent stock depth across brands
non_price_benefits.why: Stock_availability is both the #1 stated need (402) and #2 objection (301) — emphasise multi-brand inventory (Pragathi, Radiance, Color On Plus, GI, polycarbonate) as a strength.

non_price_benefits.title: Wide product range under one roof
non_price_benefits.why: 12+ distinct top products (roofing sheets, Color On Plus, screws, coils, purlins, polycarbonate) let customers consolidate orders instead of sourcing from multiple vendors.

top_questions.question: What is the rate for [sheet/screw/coil type]?
top_questions.answer_tip: Confirm exact spec (brand, thickness, colour) and share a written rate/quote immediately on the call rather than promising to send it later.

top_questions.question: Is [colour/thickness/size] in stock right now?
top_questions.answer_tip: Check live stock before answering; if unavailable, immediately offer the closest available alternative instead of just saying 'will check'.

top_questions.question: Can delivery/vehicle arrive by [specific time]?
top_questions.answer_tip: Give a firm, specific delivery commitment and proactively update the customer if timing changes rather than waiting for them to follow up.

top_questions.question: Has my payment/balance been received or confirmed?
top_questions.answer_tip: Have accounts status readily accessible so reps can confirm payment on the call, avoiding repeated chase-up calls.

top_questions.question: Can I get credit terms instead of paying upfront?
top_questions.answer_tip: Explain the credit evaluation process clearly and set expectations on timeline; escalate promptly rather than leaving it open-ended.

top_questions.question: Is there a price increase coming — should I order now?
top_questions.answer_tip: Be transparent about the effective date and encourage timely booking without guaranteeing undisclosed rates.

top_questions.question: Can you send the quote/photo/diagram on WhatsApp?
top_questions.answer_tip: Send it during the call itself; this closes the gap where 207 calls had no quote sent at all.

top_questions.question: Do you have a branch or can you deliver near [Kerala/Theni/Salem]?
top_questions.answer_tip: Be upfront about current service area and offer practical alternatives such as transport partner arrangements rather than leaving it unresolved.
